why.text: An Atlantic-continental basin with mild temperatures, fair rainfall, plenty of sun and acid soils gives fresh, mineral wines.

styles.text: Fruity or floral whites and rosados; silky, fresh reds with mineral notes and oak when aged.

climate.text: Atlantic-continental transition in a tectonic basin: mild temperatures, fairly abundant rain, many hours of sun.

why.text: Long winters, short summers, about 500 mm of rain, strong sun and poor soils, plus Prieto Picudo, give aromatic wines.

styles.text: Whites of Albarín Blanco, Verdejo and Godello; Prieto Picudo rosados; fleshy, aromatic reds, also aged.

climate.text: Continental: long, harsh winter, short summer alternating very hot dry days with cold ones, about 500 mm rain, much sun.

why.text: Extreme continental climate with sharp day-night swings and altitude slow ripening, giving Tinta del País wines rich in polyphenols and acidity.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; the reds stand up well to long ageing in oak barrels.

climate.text: Extreme continental, with a strong temperature contrast between day and night; altitude is a key factor.

why.text: A dry Mediterranean-continental climate and deep, well-drained poor soils let Prieto Picudo ripen and give red-fruited wines with a slight spritz.

styles.text: Fruity whites with aniseed notes; very fruity rosados; red-fruited reds, also aged.

climate.text: Extreme, arid Mediterranean-continental climate with low rainfall.

soil.text: Poor, infertile but deep, well drained and aerated.

why.text: Vines along the Pisuerga, 30 % of them over 60 years old, ripen intensely with balanced acidity and sugar, suiting aged wines.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, young or aged; also sweet wines and quality sparkling, white or rosé.

climate.text: Valley midway down the Pisuerga, between the cold climate upstream and the milder one at its mouth.

why.text: Tempranillo in a high, strongly continental climate with big temperature swings gains balanced acidity and sweet tannins, suited to ageing.

styles.text: Rosados with lively colour and fruit; young reds fruity and intense, aged reds complex and elegant.

climate.text: Strongly continental: big yearly and daily temperature swings, especially at ripening, low rainfall and high average altitude.

why.text: High, dry, continental-Mediterranean vineyards on clay with pebbles give Tempranillo wines rich in phenols, fresh and mineral.

styles.text: Rosados and young or aged reds; the reds show some mineral tones.

climate.text: Mediterranean with continental influence, average altitude above 800 m: long cold winters, warm dry summers, little rain, large daily swings.

soil.text: Medium texture, high in clay, with gravel and rounded stones.

why.text: Harsh winters, hot sun, iron-rich sandy-loam soils and old bush vines give very deeply coloured, high-alcohol wines.

styles.text: Whites (some barrel-fermented) and rosados; structured, tannic reds with ripe fruit and lower acidity than elsewhere.

climate.text: Extremely cold winters, many hours of sun and extreme temperatures.

soil.text: Sandy loam, neutral pH, little organic matter and rich in iron.

why.text: Alluvial soils, 350 to 400 mm rain, harsh winters, spring frost and old vines give very ripe grapes and deeply coloured, structured reds.

styles.text: Aromatic whites (some barrel-fermented), claretes and rosados; tannic, long-lived reds, also aged.

climate.text: Mediterranean, strongly continental: 350 to 400 mm rain, dry summers, harsh winters, large day-night swings, spring frost.

soil.text: Deep alluvial soils, poor in organic matter.

why.text: A high plateau, 700 to 870 m, with big day-night swings lets grapes gain sugar while keeping acidity.

styles.text: Whites, rosados, reds, quality sparkling and fortified (vino de licor) wines.

climate.text: Continental by altitude: long cold winters, late spring frost, hot dry summers, 400 to 430 mm rain, mean 11.5 °C.

soil.text: Brown soils on stony deposits: quartzite pebbles, reddish clays and sands; marls and limestone in places.

why.text: Canyon vineyards on granite and slate, warmer and wetter than the rest of the region, give Juan García wines with structure and softness.

styles.text: Whites, rosados, orange wines and reds, young or aged; reds are rich in polyphenols with ripe fruit aromas.

climate.text: Sub-humid Mediterranean, warmer and wetter than the region: 575 to 800 mm rain; canyon valleys about 5 °C warmer than the plateau.

soil.text: Acid granite and slate soils: silty sand, stony, shallow (about 30 cm), poor in lime and organic matter.

why.text: A mild, damp Mediterranean microclimate, terraced slopes and acid slate soils give Rufete wines of medium-high alcohol, minerality and long life.

styles.text: Fruity whites with medium-high body; medium-structure rosados; long-lived reds suited to keeping.

climate.text: Particular microclimate: mild, humid Mediterranean, with vineyards on terraced slopes.

why.text: Mostly old Garnacha vines on south-facing granite slopes, some above 1,000 m, give fresh wines despite hot, dry summers.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, young and barrel-aged; reds age well.

climate.text: Mediterranean with a continental touch: hot, dry summers, short mild winters, 400 to 800 mm of rain, mean 12 to 15 °C.

soil.text: Sandy loam over granite, slightly acid and poor in organic matter; some schist.

altitude.text: Some plots above 1,000 m; vines mostly on south-facing slopes.
